強いAI同士の対局から測った、カルカソンヌの先手の有利さ・得点源・逆転の起きやす: First-player advantage, where the points come from, how often games turn around, and what each tile is worth in Carcassonne, measured from games between strong AIs, compared with chess, Go and other games.
カルカソンヌは、チェスや囲碁に比べて研究がほとんど進んでいないゲームです。このペ: Compared with chess or Go, Carcassonne has barely been studied. For this page, the strongest AI on this site played {{games}} games against itself, and we measured the first-player advantage, where points come from, how often games turn around, what each tile is worth, and more. We also compare Carcassonne with chess, Go, shogi and other games.

Common road tiles are worth little on their own, but how you use them still matters, for example by not filling the spaces around your opponent's cities and monasteries.

With the same tiles, the same player won only {{same_winner}} of the time (100% if the tiles decided everything, 50% if they did not matter at all). About {{deck_corr}} of the spread in final margins can be put down to the tile order.

<span class=\"no\">9</span>先手の有利をなくすには: 9How to remove the first-player advantage
囲碁では、先に打つ黒の有利を消すために、白に最初から点を足す「コミ」があります。: In Go, White receives “komi”, extra points that offset Black’s advantage of moving first. To see whether the same works in Carcassonne, we changed the rules and had the AI play at least {{fair_games}} games under each.

後手に最初から何点あげると、先手の勝率がどうなるか（試算）: First player’s score for each starting bonus given to the second player (estimate)
4点は「強い人どうし」の数字です。慣れていない人どうしでは先後の差がもっと小さい: 4 points is the figure for strong players. Between beginners the first-player edge may be smaller, so starting with 2 or 3 points is fine too.
いちばんの理由は枚数です。開始タイルを除く71枚を交互に置くので、先手は<b c: The main reason is the tile count. The 71 tiles after the start tile are placed in turn, so the first player places {{first_tiles}} and the second player {{second_tiles}}. The first player also places the very last tile. Removing one tile so both place the same number almost erased the gap (section 9). Draws are rare: {{draw}}.
友だちや家族と1局だけ遊ぶときは、始める前に山札から1枚を見ないで箱に戻すと（2: When you play a single game with friends or family, put one tile back in the box unseen before you start (35 tiles each). That almost erases the first-player edge.
後手の得点コマを4点の位置に置いてから始める方法でも、差は誤差の範囲まで縮みます: Starting the second player’s scoring marker on 4 also shrinks the gap to within the margin of error.
先手の有利さは、チェス（白の得点率 約55%）と同じくらいかやや大きめです。囲碁: The first-player edge is about the same as in chess (White scores about 55%) or slightly larger. Unlike Go, there is no komi to balance it; tournaments only award ties to the second player (section 9).
大会ルール「同点は後手の勝ち」では: Tournament rule: “ties go to the second player”
カルカソンヌの公式ルールでは、同点なら勝ちを分け合います。一方、<a href=: Under the standard rules, tied players share the victory. But at the Japanese Championship and the German championship, a tie is a win for the second player. The “If ties go to the second player” column in the table counts games this way. Under the current rules the first player then wins {{tie_fp}} (or scores {{tie_base}} when a draw counts as half a win). Because draws are rare to begin with, this lowers the first player's rate by only {{tie_drop}} points, so almost all of the first-player edge remains. Our estimate: if ties go to the second player and the second player also starts with 3 points, the first player wins {{tie_k3}}; with 4 points, {{tie_k4}}, roughly even.
大会のように「同点は後手の勝ち」にしても、先手の有利はほとんど変わりません。引き: Even the tournament rule “ties go to the second player” barely changes the first-player edge, because draws almost never happen.
